solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: City's query regarding morality of monk

parts.note: a question opening 'Is ...?' supplies the word is
a lama is a Buddhist monk of Tibet
bad is the moral verdict asked about: is the monk good or bad?

explanation.surface: Someone wonders aloud whether a holy man's conduct is wicked, framed as a city's question.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as the question 'Is lama bad?', a query about a monk's morality; the 's after 'City' just links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamabad is the capital city of Pakistan.

clue.text: Contribution from leader at home being promoted

indicators.note: promoted in a down answer means moved higher up the column

parts.note: Vladimir Putin is the Russian leader
in means at home

explanation.surface: A national leader at home being moved up a rank makes a contribution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being promoted' lifts IN to the top of PUTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An input is something put in, a contribution of effort, ideas or resources.

clue.text: Performer friend spun atop reindeer

indicators.note: atop means placed above in a down answer, so it comes first
spun means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a pal is a friend
Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer

explanation.surface: A friend twirls while riding on one of Santa's reindeer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spun' turns PAL into LAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap dancer is an entertainer who performs erotic dances for seated customers.

clue.text: Nearly too much said about knack for making money

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned round into a new order
nearly means one letter short, so the word too loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comment that too much has almost been said about someone's flair for profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' cuts TOO to TO; 'about' rearranges TO + MUCH + SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: King Midas turned all he touched to gold, so his touch is proverbial for making money easily.

clue.text: Direct route from empty birdcage cat initially avoided

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outside letters
initially avoided means the first letter is left out

parts.note: a feline is a cat

explanation.surface: A bird takes the shortest way out of an empty cage, having dodged the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves BE of 'birdcage'; 'initially avoided' drops F from FELINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a beeline is to go straight towards something, as bees were thought to fly home.

clue.text: Strip of road holding record that lasts a while

indicators.note: holding means the road contains the record

parts.note: a drive is a road
an EP, extended play, is a record that runs longer than a single

explanation.surface: A stretch of road contains a long-lasting record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' looks like a noun, a strip of road; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip someone of something is to take it away from them, to dispossess them.

clue.text: Growth in borders of poppy crop returned

indicators.note: returned means the combined letters are sent back the other way
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to lop is to cut back or crop

explanation.surface: A gardener finds something growing along the edges of a poppy field when the crop comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders of' takes PY from 'poppy'; add LOP and 'returned' reverses PYLOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyp is a small abnormal growth of tissue, as in the nose or colon.

clue.text: Singer with Indian accompaniment hasn't left

indicators.note: hasn't left means the letter L, for left, is missing

parts.note: pilaf is spiced rice served alongside Indian dishes

explanation.surface: A vocalist accompanied by Indian musicians is still on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the standard abbreviation for left.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Piaf was the celebrated French chanteuse.

clue.text: Desert pasture extremely valuable

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or pasture

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremes, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Grazing land in a desert would be hugely precious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' is a noun in the surface but a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave is to abandon or go away from, as a soldier deserts a post.

clue.text: Events assistant fixes female on sign

indicators.note: fixes means holds in place, so the assistant wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant

indicators.note: on in a down answer means placed above

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
an omen is a sign

explanation.surface: An aide sets up a woman for her star sign reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are occurrences or observable happenings.

clue.text: Priest wearing black and white sent by Tube

indicators.note: something worn sits inside its wearer, so the priest goes inside

parts.note: pied means patched in black and white, like a magpie

explanation.surface: A cleric in monochrome robes is dispatched across London on the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' looks like the London Underground; here it is a pipe, so 'sent by Tube' is sent along pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something piped is conveyed through a tube or pipe, like water or gas.

clue.text: Some led an Alps expert around area for a walk

indicators.note: around here signals the run is read back to front
some of the words means a run of their letters is taken out

explanation.surface: A group is guided by a mountain specialist in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks EDANALPSE out of 'led an Alps expert' and 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a long open level promenade, often by the sea, built for strolling.

clue.text: Essence of co-operation lost as Met trashed Priti

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Goodwill vanished when the Metropolitan Police savaged Priti Patel, the former Home Secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' is padding linking the definition to the anagram of AS MET PRITI.
explanation.definitionFit: Team spirit is the shared morale and willingness to work together that underpins co-operation.

clue.text: Danish export sex cryptically!

indicators.note: cryptically, in crossword fashion, the word over is cut to O, its cricket scorecard abbreviation

parts.note: leg-over is British slang for sex

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark that Denmark's famous product is somehow sexual.
explanation.walkthrough: Slang 'leg-over' gives LEG + OVER, and O is the cricket abbreviation for an over, a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: The interlocking toy bricks are made by a company based in Billund, Denmark.

clue.text: Aged fellow punches red-headed man with the 3

indicators.note: punches means breaks into, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: ginger describes red hair
old means aged

explanation.surface: An elderly chap thumps a redhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the 3' points to 3 Down, the knack of turning things to gold; Goldfinger is the Bond villain obsessed with gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Auric Goldfinger in Ian Fleming's novel is a gold-hoarding villain with a seemingly golden touch.

clue.text: Carbohydrate source oddly grew

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters of the word source are kept

parts.note: rose is a past tense meaning grew or increased

explanation.surface: A source of carbohydrate grew in a strange way.
explanation.definitionFit: Sucrose is ordinary table sugar, a carbohydrate made of glucose and fructose.

clue.text: Idle bunch hit security personnel leaving university

parts.note: to slug is to hit hard

indicators.note: leaving means the university letter departs from the word

parts.note: guards are security staff

explanation.surface: A lazy group strikes the security staff as a student quits.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggards are lazy people, so a group of them is an idle bunch.

clue.text: Call up vet's centre having wounded avocet

indicators.note: the centre of the three-letter word vet is its middle letter
wounded means damaged, so the bird's letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone phones the animal clinic after a wading bird has been injured.
explanation.walkthrough: E, the centre of 'vet's', then VOCATE from 'avocet', jumbled by 'wounded'.
explanation.definitionFit: To evocate is to summon or evoke, as a spirit or a memory.

clue.text: Uninterested adult on course recalled quote

indicators.note: on in a down answer puts the adult above

parts.note: A is the film classification for adult
a path is a course or route

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A grown-up on a course remembered a quotation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns CITE into ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathetic means showing no enthusiasm or concern, the same as uninterested.

clue.text: Rutte possibly hosts starts of campaigns here

definitions.text: Rutte possibly hosts starts of campaigns here

indicators.note: hosts means the jumbled name takes the other letters inside it
possibly means the name could be rearranged into something else
the starts of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Dutch leader Mark Rutte may launch his election campaigns in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: UTRET (Rutte jumbled, signalled by 'possibly') takes in C and H, the starts of 'campaigns here'; the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Utrecht is a Dutch city, a plausible base for a Netherlands prime minister's campaigning.

clue.text: Old Greek wine is finally imported by America

indicators.note: imported by means the letters are taken inside

parts.note: the US, America, read with its article

indicators.note: finally means the last letters of the words are taken

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek vintage ends up shipped into the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America' here is read with its article, the US; the last letters of 'wine is' split it two letters in.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the hero of Greek myth who slew the Minotaur.

clue.text: State of Ford seen on films

definitions.meaning: a US state in the Midwest
Harrison Ford played the archaeologist Jones in a film series

explanation.surface: A remark on the condition of a Ford car shown in movies.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a US state, and Indiana Jones is Harrison Ford's best-known screen role.

clue.text: Ten bolt kits faulty, evaluation on the cards?

indicators.note: faulty means defective, so the letters are arranged wrongly and must be put right

explanation.surface: Defective kits of ten bolts each may be heading for an assessment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the cards' looks like 'likely'; the test literally uses cards printed with blots.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rorschach psychological assessment shows a subject cards of symmetrical ink shapes.

clue.text: Seizure in back of Flying Scotsman

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Rab is a Scottish short form of Robert, as in Rab C. Nesbitt

explanation.surface: Someone is grabbed at the rear of the famous Flying Scotsman steam train.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flying Scotsman is a celebrated London-to-Edinburgh train, which disguises 'Scotsman' as part of a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A grab is a sudden snatch or seizure of something.

clue.text: Acceptable to support Kate on Radio 4 for so long

indicators.note: to support in a down answer means to go underneath

parts.note: Kate Adie, the BBC reporter, presents From Our Own Correspondent on Radio 4
U means upper class, hence socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone listens to Kate on the radio for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a stretch of time; it is the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for goodbye, just as so long is an informal farewell.

clue.text: Evenings after work with small entitled men

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
knights carry the title Sir, so they are men with a title

explanation.surface: Little titled men gather in the evenings once the working day is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeknights are the evenings Monday to Friday, which follow the working day.

clue.text: Raised hard in country school

indicators.note: raised in a down answer means read upwards, so reversed
in means the hard letter goes inside the country

parts.note: Laos is a country in Southeast Asia
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone brought up tough at a rural school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns LAOHS upside down in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: A school of fish is a large group swimming together.

clue.text: See 19
Artist regularly in shed (that guy will make trouble)

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of in shed is taken

parts.note: he'll is the contraction of he will

explanation.surface: A painter is working steadily in a shed while someone warns that a man will cause bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes ISE from 'in shed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise hell is an idiom for causing a noisy disturbance or a lot of trouble.

clue.text: Turn on good film to see beginning

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the turn comes at the end

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's film about an alien
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Someone switches on a good film to watch the opening.
explanation.definitionFit: The get-go is an informal phrase for the very start, as in 'from the get-go'.

clue.text: This may require a double hamper

definitions.meaning: a dangerous film action sequence often uses a stand-in for the star
to hamper growth is to hold it back or impede it

explanation.surface: A puzzle that seems to ask about a picnic basket needing a twin.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunt in films is often performed by a stunt double, and to stunt means to stop growth.

clue.text: Mocking island state involved in sham trials

indicators.note: involved in means the following pieces go inside the jumbled word
sham means fake, so the letters of trials are falsified into another order

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: An island nation becomes embroiled in rigged court cases.
explanation.walkthrough: SATIRL, the anagram of 'trials', takes in I and CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Satirical writing uses ridicule and irony to mock its targets.
